prompt: Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: production game HUD damage-number bitmap sprite sheet, ten glyph sprites for a flamboyant futuristic spaceship combat game. Create an ORIGINAL, cohesive set of custom artistic numerals. Exact characters, once each: top row 0 1 2 3 4; bottom row 5 6 7 8 9. Grid is exactly FIVE equal-width columns by TWO equal-height rows; one numeral centered within each invisible cell, generous equal transparent padding, no touching or overlap. All ten digits share the same cap height, baseline, stroke weight, forward italic slant about 12 degrees, and lighting. Style: premium action-game damage typography, heavy and compact, powerful forward-swept calligraphic energy expressed with sharp angular terminals, confident blade-cut strokes and small intentional chisel notches. Readable large solid interiors and open counters; 0 must clearly read as zero, 1 a number with a substantial foot, 6/8/9 distinct. Not a plain UI font, not handwriting, not thin script, not gothic. Restrained faceted silver-white face, very subtle gray internal bevel, graphite black keyline with thin white-silver outer edge, tiny directional hard shadow; grayscale artwork so it can be tinted cyan/amber/orange in the game. Orthographic front view; consistent flat 2D sprite orientation. No floating sparkles, no speed lines outside the glyph silhouette, no colored glow, no colored backgrounds, no decoration between cells. TRUE TRANSPARENT BACKGROUND with clean alpha, no checkerboard baked into image. Only the ten numerals; no labels, no frame, no title, no alphabet, no branding, no watermark. Landscape sprite sheet, approximately 5:2 aspect ratio. Each numeral must remain crisp and distinguishable when reduced to 28-44 pixels high.
processing: tools/pipeline/pack_damage_digits.py: alpha-based glyph separation, crop, common 192px cap-height, 10 individual sprites plus padded atlas; source alpha preserved.
